title: Equivalence edges in a functor simplicial set are detected at vertices
statement: Use quasicategories, equivalence edges and the internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, let $K$ be any small simplicial set, let $F,G:K\to\mathcal C$ be diagrams, and let $\tau:F\to G$ be an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, equivalently a map $K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$ with these endpoints. Then $\tau$ is an equivalence edge if and only if for every vertex $k\in K$ its component $\tau|_{\{k\}\times\Delta^1}:F(k)\to G(k)$ is an equivalence edge of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4 (Kerodon Tag 01DK), read online on 2026-10-17, including its reference to Proposition 4.4.4.9. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag; no Stacks statement of this quasicategorical result was found. WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, with its degreewise internal-hom definition from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. First $H$ is a quasicategory. A horn $\Lambda_i^n\to H$, $0<i<n$, transposes to $K\times\Lambda_i^n\to\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] to $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ (and interchange the product factors). The first inclusion is inner anodyne by the stated lifting-class definition, since every inner fibration lifts it. The second is degreewise injective. The resulting inclusion $K\times\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^n$ therefore lifts against $\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$, which is an inner fibration by quasicategory horn filling. Transposing this filler supplies the required inner simplex in $H$.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, via Proposition 4.4.4.9 (023A) and Lemma 4.4.4.8 (01DP); explicit inverse-triangle expansion by the worker.

proof.text: If $\tau$ is an equivalence in $H$, choose an inverse edge and its two inverse $2$-simplices, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Restriction to $\{k\}\times\Delta^r$ for $r=1,2$ sends the inverse edge and both triangles to inverse data for $\tau_k$ in $\mathcal C$: it preserves every face and degeneracy by the internal-hom formula. Thus every $\tau_k$ is an equivalence. This direction uses no converse pointwise criterion.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, via Proposition 4.4.4.9 (023A) and Lemma 4.4.4.8 (01DP); explicit inverse-triangle expansion by the worker.

proof.text: Conversely assume every $\tau_k$ is an equivalence. Form a map $\Lambda_0^2\to H$ on vertices $(F,G,F)$ by specifying edge $01$ to be $\tau$ and edge $02$ to be the degenerate identity edge of $F$. These two edges agree at vertex $0$, so the degreewise product formula transposes this map to $K\times\Lambda_0^2\to\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension] with $Q=\mathcal C$, $A=\varnothing$, $B=K$, $n=2$. Its distinguished component at each vertex of $B$ is exactly $\tau_k$, hence equivalent by hypothesis. The extension $K\times\Delta^2\to\mathcal C$ transposes to a $2$-simplex $T$ in $H$. Its edge $12$ defines $\sigma:G\to F$ and its other edges are $01=\tau$, $02=\mathrm{id}_F$. Thus $T$ is the first required inverse triangle.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, via Proposition 4.4.4.9 (023A) and Lemma 4.4.4.8 (01DP); explicit inverse-triangle expansion by the worker.

proof.text: Produce the second triangle for this same $\sigma$, without selecting unrelated pointwise inverses. On the three faces of $\Lambda_0^3$ specify face $012$ to be $T$, face $013$ to be $s_1\tau$ (vertices $F,G,G$, edges $01=03=\tau$, $13=\mathrm{id}_G$), and face $023$ to be $s_0\tau$ (vertices $F,F,G$, edges $02=\mathrm{id}_F$, $03=23=\tau$). The overlaps of these faces are respectively edges $01$, $02$, $03$; the displayed values agree exactly, so they define a simplicial map $\Lambda_0^3\to H$. Transpose and apply [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension] again with $Q=\mathcal C$, $A=\varnothing$, $B=K$, now $n=3$. Its distinguished edges are still precisely $\tau_k$, with no condition on $\sigma_k$ or on the edges of $K$. Transpose the extension back to a $3$-simplex in $H$. Its face $123$ has vertices $(G,F,G)$ and edges $12=\sigma$, $23=\tau$, $13=\mathrm{id}_G$, giving the second inverse triangle.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, via Proposition 4.4.4.9 (023A) and Lemma 4.4.4.8 (01DP); explicit inverse-triangle expansion by the worker.

proof.text: The edge $\sigma$ from step 3 and the triangles $012$ and $123$ constructed in steps 3 and 4 witness both inverse equations for $\tau$. By the equivalence-edge definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $\tau$ is an equivalence in $H$. Together with step 2 this proves the asserted equivalence for every small simplicial set $K$.
